- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a5e710fb9b5bd973d44f9a5d3466d94ddaf4fa2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ebde82bd8235cc5593b323def4883c3f1dc3b7f6` — the merge of head `1418799698e8bde70ea4f94b0799a9d688f5e3c7` into base `5a5e710fb9b5bd973d44f9a5d3466d94ddaf4fa2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin ebde82bd8235cc5593b323def4883c3f1dc3b7f6 && git checkout ebde82bd8235cc5593b323def4883c3f1dc3b7f6
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1418799698e8bde70ea4f94b0799a9d688f5e3c7`
Rendered by the isolated at-tier contract reviewer spawned by the `domain:spec` seat 3 PM (seat post #18883); the authorship pair sits beside the verdict below.

Head verified with `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/19419/head` at 2026-09-20T18:31:17Z (the PR object was not trusted for it); `origin/main` read `5a5e710fb9` at the same instant, merge-base `0870fb5418`, 6 files +386/−53. Every reading below was taken in a dedicated detached worktree at that head after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (exit 0) and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` (exit 0, 18:36:23Z). This clone is shallow (graft `ae8edd2c4f`); no reading here is a history question. Nothing from the PR body, the dev report or the seat was taken as evidence — each claim below was re-measured, and where it was not, it is listed under NOT MEASURED.

### Zone 1 — the vendor premise: HOLDS, re-read first-hand

`packages/spec` resolves zod **4.4.3** exactly: `createRequire` from `packages/spec/src/index.ts` → `node_modules/.pnpm/zod@4.4.3/node_modules/zod/package.json`, `packages/spec/node_modules/zod` symlinks to the same directory, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec why zod` reports `Found 1 version of zod` (exit 0). The lockfile's second version, 4.6.1, is reached only through `better-call`/`better-auth`; `packages/spec` never sees it. In that 4.4.3 `v4/core/schemas.js`, `handleCatchall` opens at 759, the skip sits at 767-770 (`if (key === "__proto__") continue;`) **above** `_catchall.run` at 779 and above the `t === "never"` branch — so neither a catchall schema nor `.strict()`'s `unrecognized_keys` list can ever see the key. `grep -n '__proto__'` on the file returns exactly 767, 769 and 1496 (`$ZodRecord`); the CJS twin `schemas.cjs` carries the same two sites at 800 and 1527. The card's whole premise reproduces in the resolved version, in the form claimed.

### Zone 2 — `__proto__` ONLY: re-derived by measurement at this position

Probed through the real exported `AssignmentConfigSchema` at HEAD and through an unguarded twin of the same shape on the same zod, with `JSON.parse` inputs (own enumerable keys), 18:38:46Z:

| top-level key | unguarded twin | HEAD schema | value round-trips |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__proto__` | silently-dropped | **refused** (`path ['__proto__']`, `code custom`, 1 issue) | n/a |
| `constructor` · `prototype` · `toString` · `valueOf` · `hasOwnProperty` · `__defineGetter__` · `isPrototypeOf` | silently-kept | silently-kept | true, all seven |

Lit controls in the same run: a config with no reserved key round-trips; nested `assignments.__proto__` is refused at `assignments.__proto__` by the #19147 guard; `__proto__` alone is refused; `Object.create(null)` with an own `__proto__` is refused; an object literal's `{ __proto__: … }` is not an own key and never reaches either loop. So the refusal set of one name is right at this position — the three names the dev claims to have measured, and four more, all reach the catchall unskipped. The reasoning was not inherited from the record guard; it holds independently here.

### Zone 3 — the pin discriminates three outcomes, and the two guards are independent in BOTH directions

Baseline at HEAD: the two pin files run **94/94** green (exit 0, 18:38:49Z). Then two ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor declared and hit exactly once, mutation proven on disk, restore proven against HEAD's blob, tree clean after each:

- **Direction 1 (the dev's): catchall guard → no-op, record guard intact.** Blob `bfe4d455` → `62f12fa8` → restored `bfe4d455`. Result **6 failed / 88 passed (94)** — exactly the three #19151 refusal pins in `builtin-node-config.test.ts` and the three `refuseCatchallProtoKey` pins in `record-proto-key-guard.test.ts`; the #17852 / #18847 record-guard pins stayed green. (The dev's own ablation ran at commit `6a553097`/`6da7725d`, where the guard file's blob was `50724ef8`; HEAD's is `bfe4d455` because the last commit changed four citation spellings in comments. Re-run here at the head under review; same reading.)
- **Direction 2 (mine): record guard → no-op, catchall guard intact.** Blob `bfe4d455` → `682c79a5` → restored. Over the two pin files plus `data/object.test.ts`: **9 failed / 282 passed (291)** — the record-guard pins at `assignments`, `fields` and the isolated `refuseRecordProtoKey`, plus the two #19151 assertions that deliberately cross-check the record guard. The three top-level catchall refusal pins and the isolated `refuseCatchallProtoKey` refusal pin stayed **green** — the new guard does not ride on the old one.

`classify()` returns `refused` / `silently-dropped` / `silently-kept` from one parse, and the unguarded CONTROL leg in the same describe must read `silently-dropped` on this zod, so a schema that refused every config or one that kept the key and reported success would both fail. The CONTROL leg was also confirmed by the probe above.

### Zone 4 — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right; the seat's `no` → `yes` correction was on the merits

- The maintainer's ruling of record on this family says it in terms — comment 5725370319 on #17852: 「Accept set narrows for three names nobody writes ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`; spec lane at-tier review; changeset `@objectstack/spec` minor」 — and 5713646497 before it: 「This is an accept-set narrowing ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`, contract review at tier」. This PR is the third site of that family performing the same act (a refusal newly added to a published parse surface, narrowing the accept set by exactly one name), and the sibling PR #19147's review record (5737516015) accepted `yes (narrowing)` for it. `yes (narrowing)` is what the ruling prescribes; the original bare `no` contradicted it.
- Order of events, all first-hand: claim written `no` at 17:11:14Z, **before any commit existed** (first commit 17:21:21Z); the dev's changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in commit `14187996` at 18:23:30Z; the PR body declares it and names the divergence at 18:27:49Z; the dev report records it as an open question at 18:29:13Z; the seat corrects the claim at 18:30:02Z with its reasons stated and the correction announced in the comment itself. The direction of pressure was the dev's argument, not a gate: a `no` here would have let a ruled accept-set narrowing land without the at-tier review the ruling orders, which is the worse of the two errors. `check-clause2-carriers --pair 19419` read exit 0 here at 18:38:32Z, both carriers hung (card and PR), claim and PR body both `yes (narrowing)`.
- **One ground the seat gave is overstated and should not be reused.** `refuseCatchallProtoKey` is exported from `packages/spec/src/shared/record-proto-key-guard.ts` but that module is not re-exported from `shared/index.ts` or any package entry, and `api-surface/` has zero entries for either guard (`check:api-surface` reports up to date). It is a module-internal export, not a public-surface addition — the same overstatement #18847's correction (5737527984) made for `refuseRecordProtoKey`. The declaration stands on the maintainer's narrowing ruling and on the family precedent, not on that ground. Recorded so a later card does not cite "new export ⇒ `yes`" as settled.
- The C5 tell the seat calls false is line 961 of `builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, the label argument `'an `assignment` node config',` — a bare string on contract source, exactly the matcher shape #19384 (open, `pm:queue`) already describes. The gate clearing was a consequence of the merits correction, not its cause.

### Zone 5 — the ledger move is one site, the ratchet did not widen

`git diff origin/main..HEAD` on `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` is one line: `assignments.out.valueType` → `out.assignments.out.valueType` under `automation/AssignmentConfig`; the `measured` block is byte-identical (`droppedRefinementSites: 569`, `publishedSchemasWithDroppedRefinements: 204`) on both sides. `build-schemas.ts` (via the build) and `check:generated` (exit 0, all 15 artifacts current, 18:40:45Z) accept it. Lit control: with the OLD path put back through the ablation tool, `build-schemas.ts --check` exits 1 naming `~ automation/AssignmentConfig: + out.assignments.out.valueType / − assignments.out.valueType` — the gate sees this exact site, and the PR's entry is the corrected one; ledger restored to blob `fdcfdcb3`, tree clean.

Landing hazard, read from the two open PRs' patches (18:33Z): #19373 touches the `measured` block and adds four `manifest.hooks.element.object` rows (lines 3-9, 61, 154, 236, 279); #19335 touches `measured` and adds `$between` rows (605, 668, 736) and rewrites `scripts/lib/dropped-refinements.ts`'s ladder. Neither touches line 386 or the `AssignmentConfig` entry, so a plain text merge is clean against either and no hand resolution is triggered by this PR. One caveat: if #19335 lands first, its new `pruned` rung could render this pipe's site path differently — the build gate will say so on this PR's next merge of `main`, and the line moves with it; not a blocker.

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` at HEAD derived **81** commands (6 paths off merge-base `0870fb54`); every one was run with its exit captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reconciled: **81 derived, 81 run, 0 UNRUN; 76 exit 0, 5 exit 3** (18:45:36Z–18:57:35Z). The five exit-3s, by each script's own contract, are PREREQUISITE NOT MET — not reds and not passes:

- `check:doc-formula-expressions` (`@objectstack/lint`) and `check:lean-entry-closure` — two the dev did not name (its closure build had already satisfied them). After `turbo run build` of the service-automation closure + `objectql` + `formula` + `lint` (21/21 tasks, exit 0), both **exit 0**: lean-entry-closure measured `@objectstack/objectql/core` import/require at 15 packages, admitted set held exactly.

So the dev's `78 exit 0 / 3 exit 3` and this `76 / 5` are the same 81 commands under two build states; no red hides in either. Beyond the derived 81: the two families `lint.yml` wired after this branch's base — `pnpm check:issue-citations` and `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` (diff-scoped), `pnpm check:merged-result` — plus `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity` (the six roster gates the derivation flags as sitting in a directory this diff touches) all **exit 0**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0, all 15 artifacts current.

Three exit-3s are PREREQUISITE NOT MET by each script's own contract, not reds: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` refuses when its positive control (the real pre-#10375 revision) is unreachable in a shallow clone; `check:type-check-debt` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` refuse against a tree with no whole-repo `dist/` (both documented as exit 3, distinct from a finding's 1). ### Other readings

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` exit 0 — **504 files / 14,754 tests** (19:08:35Z); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exit 0 (tsc + scripts + test layer, 18:46:42Z); repo-wide `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) exit 0 (19:10:17Z).

- Census for the changeset's `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: **0** authored `__proto__` keys in non-test sources here (the 5 grep hits are all comments about `__proto__: null` literals) and **0** in the `objectui` sibling at `8b446f5`; lit control 100 `assignment` node declarations in 26 files here, 12 in 5 files there — the dev's `11 files there` was not reproduced at this sibling checkout, the zero was.
- `refuseRecordProtoKey`'s message bytes and its two consumers (`ObjectSchema.fields`, `assignments`) are unchanged; no consumer anywhere reads `.shape`/`.extend`/`.pick` on `AssignmentConfigSchema` (a pipe would break those at runtime despite the cast) — the only consumers are the schemaless registry map and `flow-node-expression-paths`, both pinned by the JSON-projection test.
